newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up on mining sector bull run.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up on mining sector bull run.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Monday, lifted by largely speculative buys in leading polymetallic miners Morococha and Atacocha, brokers said.
They said the market would likely continue rising Tuesday.

Monday, the General Index rose 0.88 percent to 1,863.5 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.68 percent to 2,725.8 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close at 1330 local time (1830 GMT). In a total of 1,824 trades, volume was a modest 22.0 million soles ($.8.3 million), brokers said.
Morococha rose 10.0 percent to 5.61 soles on volume of 677,000 shares, while Atacocha jumped 7.1 percent to 1.81 soles on volume of 798,000 shares.

These climbs were due to small investors positioning themselves in the attractive stocks that have led this month's mining sector bull run, brokers said. Since the start of the year, miners' liquid labor shares have gained almost 120 percent, according to the exchange's figures.
But brokers said Peru's generally better economic performance this year were underscoring the market's overall upward trend.

"The interest in shares is based on the change in the economic trend, given that we have entered a better period for the economy that wakes up investors' interest," said Jose Luis Cueto of ING Baring in Lima.

After a longer-than-expected slowdown of the economy last year, the country's gross domestic product (GDP) has increased dramatically so far in 1997. Year-on-year GDP for the first quarter was 4.8 percent compared with 0.6 percent in the same period in 1996, according to latest government figures.
